quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: You do not need to leave as much space when following a motorcycle as when following a car.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop faster than cars in dry conditions. You should stay 3 to 4 seconds behind a motorcycle to give the rider time to react in an emergency.

questions.question: You come to an intersection blocked by traffic. You should:

options.text: Go slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through completely.
Honk your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through completely.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is backed up on the other side and you cannot get all the way through. Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: You notice a problem with your vehicle that could affect safe driving. You should:

options.text: Fix the problem when you have money for it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the problem right away.
questions.explanation: Fix any problem that could affect safe driving before you drive the vehicle.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you must:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Let traffic and pedestrians pass, then go only when it is safe. At railroad crossings, a flashing red light means a train is near. Wait until the lights stop flashing and all warnings are off before crossing.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead has a sharp right turn followed by a sharp left turn.

questions.question: In fog, you should use high beam headlights to see better.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: In fog, use low beam headlights or fog lights instead of high beams.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must go either right or left.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must go either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a Y intersection ahead. Choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: Your accelerator sticks while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: Keep your eyes on the road. Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly. When safe, pull to the side of the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: Drive slower than the posted speed limit when:

options.text: You are entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Slow down when the road is wet or slippery, when visibility is poor, or when anything else makes conditions less than perfect. You can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions, even if you are at the speed limit.

questions.question: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at:
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show exactly where you must stop.

questions.question: A good rule for passing other vehicles is:

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Move to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash lights and honk to tell other drivers you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each time you pass a vehicle, there is a higher chance of a crash. If you drive faster than other traffic, you will need to pass many vehicles. Drive at the same speed as other traffic, within the speed limit, and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: Mixing drugs with alcohol:

options.text: Increases your chance of causing a crash.
Is no more dangerous than drinking alcohol alone.
Makes alcohol less harmful to your driving.
Does not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases your chance of causing a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can harm your brain function and make driving unsafe. Mixing alcohol with other drugs greatly increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: Five-sided signs mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Five-sided signs show you are in a school zone. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians near schools.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive with caution.

questions.question: Sometimes 10 mph is too fast for safe driving.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Drive slower than the speed limit when weather, traffic, or visibility is poor. In some cases, you may need to drive as slowly as 10 miles per hour.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. You should:

options.text: Signal the other driver when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when another driver passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and reduce your speed to help the passing vehicle move back into the right lane safely.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.correctAnswerText: In the shade.
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be careful on shaded roads near trees or buildings. These areas freeze before other roads and dry last.

questions.question: You may cross a dashed white line:

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You may cross dashed lines to pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When leaving a driveway to enter a street, you:

options.text: Must drive slowly to give vehicles and pedestrians time to move.
Must honk so vehicles and pedestrians know to move for you.
Must stop and make sure no pedestrians or vehicles are coming before entering.
Can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and make sure no pedestrians or vehicles are coming before entering.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway. Yield to any vehicles or pedestrians. You must stop before crossing the sidewalk. Not stopping is illegal.

questions.question: What should you do if your right wheels leave the road?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, do not panic. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the road. Keep both hands on the wheel and make a small steering correction. Check for other traffic before returning to the road.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your vehicle's antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels during winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are the best choice for your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter is the hardest driving season and requires extra care. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often. Snow tires improve your vehicle's grip on slippery roads.

questions.question: Bicycles on the road:

options.text: Must always yield to motor vehicles.
Do not have to follow traffic rules.
Are not a concern for drivers.
Have the same rights and duties as motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have the same rights and duties as motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles. Motor vehicle drivers must respect bicyclists' rights on the road.

questions.question: You may honk your horn when you:

options.text: Have lost control of your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: Downward-pointing triangular signs mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-pointing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. When the road is clear of traffic and pedestrians and it is safe, you may proceed.

questions.question: When you see this sign, it means:

options.text: Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show that the road curves sharply in the direction of the arrow. In this case, the curve goes left. You may see several chevron signs through a curve.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, drivers of small vehicles should prepare for:

options.text: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles off course. Be ready to steer correctly when passing large vehicles moving at high speed.

questions.question: On a highway with two solid yellow lines, you may:

options.text: Cross only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross to pass other vehicles if no traffic is coming.
Cross only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction. You may only cross them to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing without flashing lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross quickly as soon as possible.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to trains at any crossing, especially without lights or gates. Make sure your entire vehicle fits on the other side before crossing. Do not shift gears while on railroad tracks—your vehicle might stall.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, it is safest to:

options.text: Change your speed to stay alert.
Drive at the same speed as other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Always drive at the same speed as traffic around you, while staying within the speed limit.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk to alert the bicyclist you are passing.
Drive in the bike lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give as much space as possible.
Speed ahead and pull in front of them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists as much space as you can. Bicyclists have less protection than car drivers and need room. Passing too fast can knock them off course.

questions.question: Is it illegal to crowd a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Crowding a motorcycle is illegal and dangerous. Never drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean drivers cannot pass.

questions.question: Should you treat a railroad crossbuck sign the same as a yield sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: A railroad crossing sign is a yield sign. You must yield to any trains and railroad equipment.

questions.question: You arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as a vehicle on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Let them pass safely, then you may go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
You can go if the way is clear.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: If you pass this sign, you are going the wrong way. You risk a head-on collision. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: What does an octagonal sign always mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop at every red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How much time passes between drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are
questions.explanation: Your BAC depends on how much you drink, time between drinks, and your weight. Your fitness level does not affect your BAC.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Talk to other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means what color light will appear next?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will appear next.

questions.question: What happens when you drive while distracted?

options.text: You react more slowly to hazards.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You react more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow your reaction time to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is always dangerous.
